analysis.title: Fixed Income Perspectives: A More Bond-Friendly Policy Mix Takes Shape
key_insights: Voya says the election changes the path of growth, not the direction. Divided government makes another large deficit-financed stimulus less likely, which should cool growth and inflation without ending the expansion.

Voya expects less upward pressure on Treasury yields and lower rate volatility, which favors duration. It says rates do not need to fall for bonds to deliver attractive returns given current starting yields.
Policy shifts on Iran and tariffs could ease inflation. A slower pace of AI/data center investment could temper growth at the margin. Voya expects lower interest rates as a result.

Securitized credit is Voya's preferred area: residential mortgage credit and consumer ABS are rated positive. Support cited includes built-up home equity, a housing shortage of roughly 3 million units and limited new supply.
Voya sees tight credit spreads as a reason to be selective. With less room to tighten, spreads are more vulnerable if growth slows more sharply than expected.
If scrutiny slows data center projects, companies may borrow less to fund construction. That would mean fewer new IG bonds and ease a supply headwind.

IG corporates were upgraded to neutral after October's spread widening. Voya sees selective value in hybrids, BBBs, banks and TMT/AI-capex beneficiaries. October IG supply was $125 billion, above expectations, helped by late-month hyperscaler deals.

High yield stays neutral: supportive fundamentals and carry are offset by tight valuations. Voya is underweight CCCs, cable/satellite, media, telecom, technology, transportation and energy E&P, and favors low-BB to mid/high-B risk.

Senior loans stay constructive but with tight valuations. October returns were negative on AI-related supply indigestion, higher oil prices and elevated inflation. CLO issuance was $12.6 billion. Voya favors low-BB and mid-single-B loans.

Agency MBS remains modestly positive tactically. Current-coupon OAS tightened 5 bp to 28 and ZV widened 1 bp to 110, both wider than 12-month averages. Tailwinds are muted organic supply, low cash-out refinancing and potential GSE purchase demand.

CLOs are mixed (tight IG tranche valuations and AI/SaaS disruption risk against floating-rate demand). Non-agency CMBS could be pressured by elevated rates, but early-cycle dynamics should limit the impact.

EM hard currency debt is neutral. October spreads widened 30 bp for corporates and 20 bp for sovereigns but remain near historical tights. Voya is overweight corporates/quasis and Latin America and underweight sovereigns, Asia, GCC and A-rated risk. Main risk is higher U.S. real rates, a stronger dollar and a more hawkish Fed.

sector_views.rationale: Upgraded to neutral after October's spread widening, with selective value in hybrids, BBBs, banks and TMT/AI-capex beneficiaries.
Supportive fundamentals and carry are offset by tight valuations. Stress is visible in CCCs, cable/satellite and lower-income consumer credits.
Strong technicals, stable fundamentals, below-average payment defaults and attractive carry, but tight valuations.
Modestly positive tactically on muted organic supply, low cash-out refinancing and potential GSE purchase demand.

sector_views.sector: Securitized credit (mortgage credit and consumer ABS)
sector_views.rationale: Built-up home equity, a roughly 3-million-unit housing shortage, shrinking forward supply and a resilient labor market.
Tight spreads are offset by resilient global growth and elevated absolute yields.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Voya expects growth to moderate as additional fiscal stimulus becomes less likely and AI investment may slow. Next release 11/25/26.
Voya expects job growth to moderate but stay positive. Next release 12/04/26.
Slower growth could push unemployment up modestly, with a slowly expanding labor force limiting the rise. Next release 12/04/26.
Limited labor availability prevents a sharp decline in wage pressure as labor demand softens. Next release 12/04/26.
Voya expects inflation to resume its downward trend as lower oil prices and easing tariffs reduce pressure. Next release 11/25/26.

risk_factors: Credit spreads are tight, so they are more vulnerable if growth slows more sharply than expected.
Pressure on lower-income consumers requires selectivity in consumer ABS and HY.
AI/SaaS disruption and AI-related supply indigestion weigh on CLOs and senior loans.
Higher U.S. real rates, a stronger dollar and a more hawkish Fed could overshadow EM fundamentals.
Agency MBS: resumed Treasury selloff, rate volatility shocks, GSE purchase execution, bank and overseas buyer hesitation, policy headlines.
vol_and_positioning: Voya expects less upward pressure on Treasury yields and reduced rate volatility.
Agency MBS risks include a resumed Treasury selloff, renewed rate volatility shocks, fast-money or REIT selling and disappointing GSE purchase execution.
geopolitical: Election backlash against the Iran war lowers the risk of further escalation, which Voya says could mean lower energy costs and inflation.
House and Senate could limit the ability to implement additional tariffs and challenge existing ones, lowering import costs.

tension_points.bull_case: A healthy economy supports credit spreads, and Voya sees continued growth backing credit.
tension_points.bear_case: With less room to tighten from current levels, spreads are more vulnerable if growth slows more sharply than expected.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth slowing more sharply than expected.

theme_stances.key_argument: Less fiscal stimulus, easing tariff and energy pressure and slower AI investment should lower yields and rate volatility while keeping growth healthy enough to support credit.
